name: Swiggy Limited
period: FY2026 (year to 31 March 2026), with the Q1 FY27 update (quarter to 30 June 2026)
evidence_note: Read in the company's own documents: the FY2026 annual report and the Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 shareholder letters. Page numbers are PDF pages.

q1.title: Swiggy Q1 FY27 shareholders' letter (30 July 2026)

bs.title: Business Standard: Swiggy shareholders approve IOCC status, cap foreign ownership at 49.5%

headline.text: A food, grocery and going-out app. The consumer apps earn the headline order value, but audited revenue is almost half B2B goods supply, and only food delivery makes a segment profit.

answers.a: Restaurant food delivery; groceries and household items from dark stores (Instamart); restaurant reservations and events (Dineout, Scenes); goods and warehousing for wholesalers and retailers (Swiggy Networks, formerly Scootsy); and early-stage experiments such as Toing and Crew.

answers.q: Which products contribute most to revenue?
answers.a: It depends on the lens. By order value: food 51%, Instamart 42%, out-of-home 7%. By audited revenue: supply chain 47%, food 34%, Instamart 17%. By profit: only food delivery (+1,041) and out-of-home (+29) earned a segment profit; the group lost 4,154.

23.5 million average monthly transacting users, about 266,000 monthly transacting restaurant partners and 649,000 delivery partners (FY26 averages). No single customer reached 10% of revenue in FY26. One did in FY25 (1,573, in the supply chain segment).

B2C by order value: the company's 'B2C GOV' is food, Instamart and out-of-home. B2B by audited revenue: the supply chain segment sells goods to wholesalers and retailers and is 47% of revenue. Merchants and brands also pay commissions and advertising on the consumer app.
Domestic only. The company says it operates solely in India (35 states and union territories) and export disclosures do not apply. Food delivery covers 720+ cities; Instamart 131 cities by Q1 FY27.
Service and trading, not manufacturing. FY26 revenue: platform services 11,927; traded goods 9,952; supply chain services 915; food sold 34. Raw material consumed was only 45.
Instamart: 1,171 dark stores covering 4.92 million sq ft at Q1 FY27. Management says utilisation is about 40% and the business can double without new stores. Orders per store per day were 1,089.

capacity.title: Capacity and utilisation: Instamart dark stores
capacity.definition: Capacity is the dark-store network. The company measures throughput as orders per active store per day and order value per sq ft of active store area, in each quarter.

rows.label: Orders per dark store per day
Order value per sq ft (per quarter)

claims.text: Management: utilisation is about 40%, and the business can comfortably double without adding stores other than for densification.
A new store takes under 90 days to open; about 75 stores are planned for Q2 FY27 (28 were added in Q1).
The top tenth of stores earn a 3 to 5% contribution margin; the most mature city is about 3%.
Stores rose from 523 to 1,143 in two years, and store area from 1.5 to 4.8 million sq ft.
If 1,089 orders a day is 40% utilisation, implied capacity is about 2,700 orders per store per day (1,089 divided by 0.40).

capacity.reading: Utilisation improved in value, not in volume. Order value per sq ft is up 39% since Q4 FY25 because the average order grew from 527 to 700, while orders per store per day fell from 1,190 to 1,093 and have been flat since.

momentum.title: Quarterly trend: growth is slowing

rows.label: B2C order value growth, year on year

momentum.reading: B2C order value growth fell from 49% to 28% in three quarters. Instamart order value grew 94% in FY26 but only 39.8% in Q1 FY27, and was flat from Q4 to Q1 (7,881 to 7,907). Users grew faster than orders, so orders per user per month fell.

sync.claim: Food delivery adjusted EBITDA crossed 1,000, 2.9% of order value.
sync.statutory: Audited segment result 1,041, which is 3.0% of order value.

sync.claim: Instamart contribution margin improved to -2.8% of order value.
sync.statutory: Audited segment result -3,063, which is -10.7% of order value. Company adjusted EBITDA margin -12.3%.
sync.why: Different measures, not a mismatch. The headline excludes fixed costs such as rent, technology, marketing and overheads.

sync.statutory: Break-even in May 2026; the quarter was -0.2%, and the segment still lost 778 in Q1 FY27.
Order value grew 45.5%. The supply chain segment grew 70% at a loss.
sync.why: Revenue outgrew demand because of low-margin B2B goods trading.

sync.statutory: Orders per store per day were 1,093 in Q4 FY26 against 1,190 a year earlier. Order value per sq ft rose 39%.
sync.why: True in value (bigger baskets), not in volume.

sync.claim: Instamart has front-loaded its stores and now focuses on using them better.
sync.statutory: Of 4,475 of share-placement money earmarked for dark stores and warehouses, none was spent in FY26.

sync.claim: Adjusted EBITDA is the headline profit measure.
sync.statutory: It excludes ESOP cost of 966 (23% of the loss) and other income, and deducts lease rentals of 607.
sync.why: A real cost is left out of the headline; rent is counted.

sync.statutory: 47% of audited revenue is the supply chain segment, which has lost money every year from FY23 to FY26.
sync.why: The consumer story describes order value, not audited revenue.

sync.claim: Cash and cash equivalents of 15,053 at March 2026.
sync.statutory: Our data provider shows 11,228 on a narrower definition.
sync.why: Definition gap of about 3,800. Valuation should state which cash it uses.

guidance.item: Instamart contribution break-even 'latest by Q1 FY27' (set at Q4 FY25, when it was -5.6%).
guidance.outcome: Break-even in May 2026; the quarter was -0.2%.
Held between zero and -1% for a couple of quarters while growth is accelerated.

guidance.item: Food delivery order value growth of 18 to 20% (excluding Toing).
guidance.outcome: 22.6% in Q4 FY26; 17.4% in Q1 FY27 (about 18% adjusted for LPG-related cancellations).

guidance.item: Food delivery adjusted EBITDA of 5% of order value over the medium term.
Instamart adjusted EBITDA break-even at about 60,000 annualised net order value (25 to 30 crore orders a quarter, against 11.5 crore now) and about 30 contribution per order.
guidance.outcome: Annualised net order value is about 23,300 now (5,817 times four), so volume must rise about 2.6 times.

guidance.item: Become an Indian-owned-and-controlled company so Instamart can own inventory (about +80 bps contribution margin).
guidance.outcome: Board approved on 23 July 2026; shareholders approved on 18 August 2026 (press). Transition expected over 2 to 4 quarters.

definitions.meaning: Value of completed orders including delivery fees, packaging and taxes, before discounts. Instamart's is measured at maximum retail price.
GOV less all discounts: what consumers actually pay. Delivered orders only.
GOV of food delivery, Instamart and out-of-home, excluding platform innovations.
Statutory revenue plus user delivery charges and user fees that are not in statutory revenue.
Profit before tax, interest, depreciation, other income, ESOP expense, exceptional items and associate losses, after deducting lease rentals.
Revenue less delivery cost, platform-funded discounts and other variable costs, as a share of GOV. Excludes fixed costs.

comparability: Statutory revenue (23,053) and adjusted revenue (24,315) differ by 1,262 of user delivery charges and fees. Check which one a source quotes.
Instamart is moving to owning inventory (board approval 23 July 2026). Reported revenue will probably jump and stop being comparable with earlier periods. Use order value for growth.
'Adjusted EBITDA' excludes ESOP and other income and deducts lease rentals, so it differs from the statutory loss by 1,283.
Order-value measures (GOV, NOV, 'NRV') are defined differently by each company and are not comparable across companies.

risks.text: GST show-cause notice of 327 on delivery charges collected for delivery partners (July 2020 to March 2022). The Karnataka High Court has stayed the proceedings. No provision is made.
Key audit matters: how platform revenue is recognised; impairment of 4,489 invested in the supply chain subsidiary plus 2,764 of loans and deposits; goodwill of 315 in out-of-home.
The supply chain segment's adjusted EBITDA was negative every year: -295, -187, -280 and -192 for FY23 to FY26.
Cash burn: 3,302 plus 670 of working capital in FY26, funded by a 10,000 share placement and the sale of a stake in Rapido (2,399).
Delivery partner supply: 612 thousand monthly transacting in Q4 FY26 against 691 thousand in Q2, which management attributes to seasonal migration and elections.

open_questions: Who buys the 9,952 of traded goods? The letter defines buyers only as wholesalers and retailers.
Why did one customer exceed 10% of revenue in FY25 and not in FY26?
Other income jumped to 266 in Q4 FY26 while realised treasury income was 79. What is the rest?
How will the inventory-led shift be accounted for, and what will it do to revenue and working capital?
Whether Q1 FY27 growth really re-accelerates, as management claims (four-week net order value growth of 10.0% against 1.0% before).

segments.name: Food delivery
segments.evidence: Order value growth guided at 18 to 20% (Q1 FY27: 17.4%); medium-term adjusted EBITDA target 5% of order value, 3.1% in Q1 FY27 (management claim).

segments.name: Instamart (quick commerce)
segments.evidence: FY26 order value +94%, flat from Q4 FY26 to Q1 FY27. Top tenth of stores earn 3 to 5% contribution margin (claim); utilisation about 40% (claim).

segments.name: Out-of-home (Dineout, Scenes)
segments.evidence: Small and about break-even. Growth and margin here are our assumptions with no company target to anchor them.

other.label: Supply chain and platform innovations
other.note: Segment results of -77 and -195. Treated as a loss that continues for 3 years then stops. Supply chain is a pass-through goods business with no order value, so no standalone value is given to it.

central.note: Share-based pay and depreciation are not allocated to segments. Together 2,183, or 3.2% of order value in FY26. We assume the share falls to 2.0% as the business scales, which is our assumption.
